request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1.)

tools.name: get_fold_detail
tools.description: Get the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown for a completed experiment run. Use this to compare fold-level consistency between runs.

output.text:
**Choice: run 4, logistic regression (all+agent features, class_weight, C=0.1). Confidence is 0.5.**

**Why logistic:**
- LightGBM (run 1) has the best mean PR-AUC at 0.7368. Logistic is at 0.6944, so the gap is 0.042.
- The fold SDs are about 0.061 to 0.064, so the gap is smaller than one SD. Under the simplicity rule, the simpler model wins.
- Random forest (run 3) is worse than both, so it is out. Run 2 is also worse than run 1 and is no simpler than logistic.

**Why I'm not more confident:**
- LightGBM beats logistic in 4 of 5 folds. The paired differences are +0.102, +0.056, +0.031, +0.030 and −0.007. That is a fairly consistent edge, even though it is below the one-SD bar.
- A reasonable reviewer could pick LightGBM instead. I picked logistic because I applied the stated rule strictly.
- Fold spread is large. Per-fold PR-AUC ranges from 0.61 to 0.80, and fold 3 is the weakest for every model I inspected. With about 500 positives in total, that spread is expected.
- I did not inspect run 3. I did not need it, since its mean is below the others.

**Possible leakage:**
- ROC-AUC is about 0.94 for every model, including a heavily regularised logistic regression. Very different model families reaching the same ceiling suggests the signal is simple. It may come from a few dominant features, such as claim volume or size.
- If so, the `PotentialFraud` label may partly be a function of those features. That could happen if the label came from a rule-based or claims-derived flag.
- Precision@50 of 0.74 to 0.78 is high for labels that are only suspicion, not confirmed fraud.
- The result therefore shows that the models reproduce the label. It does not show they find real fraud.
- Before anyone acts on the queue, I would check three things:
  - how the label was produced;
  - whether the folds respect time or provider grouping, given the 13-month claims window;
  - which features drive the predictions.

**Stop:** true. No rounds are left, and the top configurations are too close for more search to separate them.
